titleTemplate.title: Page title pattern
titleTemplate.description: How page titles are written: {name} is the page's part (a product's or category's own SEO title, else its title pattern), {business} the name in titles. The name in titles is never added twice: a part that already holds it gets nothing added. A title set to be used as written replaces the whole pattern.

brandName.title: Name in titles
brandName.description: The name {business} and {storeName} stand for in page titles and descriptions. Empty: your business name.

alternateName.title: Other site name
alternateName.description: Another name people know your website by (an acronym or a shorter name), given to search engines with the site name. Empty: none.

homeTitle.title: Home page title
homeTitle.description: Your home page's title, used as written. Empty: the name in titles (your business name unless Name in titles is set).

homeDescription.title: Home page description
homeDescription.description: Your home page's meta description, used as written. Empty: the default description.

businessType.title: Business type in structured data
businessType.description: What your home page tells search engines your business is: OnlineStore, or any schema.org local business type (LocalBusiness, Store, ClothingStore, Bakery, Pharmacy …). A local business type is given at your pickup point (Delivery zones: its address and hours; hours written like Mo-Fr 09:00-17:00, one line per group of days, are also given as opening hours); without a pickup address and hours, an OnlineStore.

socialProfiles.title: Social profiles
socialProfiles.description: The https addresses of your business's profiles on other sites (social networks, review sites), given to search engines with your business.

productTitle.title: Product title
productTitle.description: A product's part of the page title ({name} of the title pattern): {name} is the product, {brand} its brand, {category} its category, {storeName} the name in titles, and the facts {price}, {minPrice}, {maxPrice}, {options}, {inStockOptions}, {conditions} and {topSpecs}, filled from the product as it is on every read. A part in square brackets is left out when one of its placeholders is empty, for example {name}[ by {brand}]. A product's own SEO title replaces it.

categoryTitle.title: Category title
categoryTitle.description: A category's part of the page title ({name} of the title pattern): {name} is the category, {category} the category above it, {storeName} the name in titles, for example Shop {name}. A category's own SEO title replaces it.

productDescription.title: Product description pattern
productDescription.description: A product's meta description when it has no SEO description of its own and no summary of 50 characters or more: {name}, {brand}, {category}, {storeName} and the facts {price} (the price or the range), {minPrice}, {maxPrice}, {options} and {inStockOptions} (the option values offered, and those in stock), {conditions} (the grades offered) and {topSpecs} (the first 3 specs), filled on every read so they never go stale. A part in square brackets is left out when one of its placeholders is empty. Empty: its description, then the default description.

categoryDescription.title: Category description pattern
categoryDescription.description: Used when a category has no SEO description of its own, before its summary and description: {name}, {category} and {storeName}, for example Browse {name} at {storeName}. A part in square brackets is left out when one of its placeholders is empty. Empty: the summary, then the description.

variantTitle.title: Variant name
variantTitle.description: How each variant is named in structured data: {name} is the product, {brand} its brand, {options} the variant's option values (Red / L), {grade} its grade. A part in square brackets is left out when one of its placeholders is empty.

pagedListings.title: Listing pages after the first
pagedListings.description: Pages 2, 3 … of a category or landing page: indexed or not indexed (noindex, follow). Each page keeps its own address as canonical either way, as search engines ask.

emptyCategories.title: Categories without products
emptyCategories.description: Not indexed (noindex, follow, and left out of the sitemap) while a category has no product shoppers can see, in it or below it, and no text of its own (a summary or description of 50 words or more), as search engines ask of empty pages; or indexed anyway.

faqMarkup.title: FAQ structured data
faqMarkup.description: Also describe the questions of products, categories, landing and glossary pages as FAQPage structured data. Google stopped showing FAQ results on May 7, 2026; other search engines may still read it. The questions are shown on your pages either way.

sitemapUrl.title: Sitemap address
sitemapUrl.description: Where your website serves the sitemap. Above the addresses per sitemap file it becomes an index of files at this address with ?file=categories, ?file=landings, ?file=products-1 …

sitemapSize.title: Addresses per sitemap file
sitemapSize.description: Above this many addresses the sitemap becomes an index of files (categories, landing pages, products-1, products-2 …). At most 15,000: with up to 10 photos per product a file then stays under the 50 MB search engines read.

defaultDescription.title: Default description
defaultDescription.description: Used when a page has no description of its own.

defaultImage.title: Default image
defaultImage.description: An https address used when a page has no image of its own.

indexNowOnSave.title: Send changes to IndexNow
indexNowOnSave.description: When a save changes a page, its address is sent to search engines through Growth's IndexNow: the product (and its earlier address after a new slug), its categories' listings, a saved category (paste the Growth token in Connections).

autoSeo.title: SEO copy when saving
autoSeo.description: On save: when staff save a product or an attribute whose SEO title, description or questions are empty, your AI provider writes them (AI copy on and its key in Connections), kept as AI copy. Without AI nothing is stored: the title and description patterns fill your pages on every read, so they never go stale. Off: nothing is written.
